## Constitution Alignment

No alignment issues. Standard-library-only, local deterministic behavior and preservation of explicit human choices are reflected in plan.md:13–29 and tasks.md:T002–T012. Unit and subprocess tests precede implementation in the task dependency graph (tasks.md:59); no Git, publication, other-consumer work or automatic acceptance is authorized (tasks.md:75).

## Unmapped Tasks

None. T001 is genuine completed CLI-design history; T002/T003 provide required setup/foundation; T004–T010 implement and test the two stories; T011/T012 supply cross-cutting validation and evidence documentation. The additional test files stay within the planned tests/ directory and split independently writable cases; they do not add an unplanned component or external dependency.

## Metrics

- Total requirements: 12 (9 functional requirements and 3 buildable success criteria).
- Total tasks: 12 (1 completed design-history row and 11 unchecked implementation rows).
- Coverage: 100% (12/12 requirements have at least one task).
- Ambiguity count: 0.
- Duplication count: 0.
- Critical issues: 0.

## Evidence and Limits

Prerequisite check passed with spec, plan and tasks available. Both Analyze hook phases were checked by parsing the registry; neither has registered hooks. All nine accepted choices remain coherent across spec.md:63–71, plan.md:68–78, the CLI contract, data model and tasks. In particular, original nonempty whitespace-only input yields LF (T004/T006), complete strict decoding precedes emission (T007/T010), and required rejection categories yield status 2/stderr/zero stdout (T008/T010). No unresolved placeholders or material dependency/parallel-writer conflicts were identified.

This is pre-implementation artifact analysis. The absence of implementation code and unchecked implementation rows is expected and does not constitute a task-generation defect. Source/wiki pre-clarification choices are explicitly historical in spec.md:59,91 and do not override recorded operator answers. No behavior tests were executed because implementation is outside this assessment.

## Next Actions

No remediation edits are indicated by this analysis. Return this clean report to the existing workflow classification path. Any later implementation, roadmap decision, Git baseline or feature acceptance requires its own authorized boundary; none was invoked here. The core remediation offer is inapplicable because there are zero issues to remediate.
